nodes.description: Elevated body temperature activates the CaV1.2 L-type calcium channel. Superimposed on the CACNA1C gain-of-function lesion, fever is hypothesized to further augment the persistent inward calcium current, acutely lowering the threshold for both ventricular arrhythmia and seizures. In a zebrafish cacna1c model this was sufficient to elicit arrhythmia and seizure-like behavior even in overtly normal heterozygotes, framing fever as an acute, modifiable exacerbating factor rather than a fixed trait. This node and its downstream edges are part of the emerging fever_exacerbated_cav1.2 hypothesis.

nodes.description: CaV1.2 is expressed in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus, where glucose-sensitive POMC-expressing neurons regulate glucose homeostasis. In mice, expressing the Timothy syndrome mutant channel only in POMC neurons reduced blood glucose excursion in a glucose tolerance test, as in the whole-body knock-in, while the wild-type channel had no effect. Serum glucagon and insulin were unchanged in these mice, so this component acts separately from the alpha-cell defect. Its contribution to hypoglycemia in patients is not established.

nodes.description: Episodic severe hypoglycemia in Timothy syndrome was long attributed to excess calcium influx in pancreatic beta cells and consequent hyperinsulinism, but that hypothesis lacked supporting data. In a CaV1.2 G406R knock-in mouse that reproduces the hypoglycemia, intrinsic beta-cell function of isolated islets was normal and serum insulin was low; the counterregulatory response was defective instead. Isolated islets secreted less glucagon at low glucose and alpha-cell mass was reduced. The same mice had raised baseline serum epinephrine, which the authors attribute to the mutant channel in adrenal chromaffin cells; that finding cuts against a simple failure of counterregulation, and its contribution is not resolved. Patient data available to the same study showed no hyperinsulinism. This component is separate from the hypothalamic POMC-neuron component: mice expressing the mutant channel only in POMC neurons had normal glucagon.
